question: Do current authoritative fish-taxonomy records support the names used for the two historical Paitan candidates, and does this resolve identification of the original survey material?
decision: The Catalog of Fishes currently treats Leiopotherapon plumbeus and Oreochromis niloticus as valid species names, matching the two names in the publisher-indexed Silliman excerpts. This is a nomenclatural cross-check only. It does not re-identify the 2009 study fish, supply missing voucher links, confirm the field date, establish current Paitan presence, or authorize public species projection.

sourceAccess.accessResult: Search-indexed species pages returned current validity statements for both names. Direct open of the catalog species pages returned HTTP 403 in this review; no local page copy was retained.
sourceAccess.paitanSource: Publisher-indexed excerpts of Paz-Alberto et al. (2009), previously reviewed in central-luzon-paitan-vaca-silliman-site-followup-20261119.json; the article PDF itself remains inaccessible by direct retrieval.

nameCrosswalk.authorityCheck: Catalog of Fishes reports the name as valid; its indexed species entry places it in Terapontidae and describes it as a Philippine freshwater endemic.
nameCrosswalk.relationToPaitanSource: The binomial matches the name explicitly stated in the Silliman discussion for Paitan Lake.
nameCrosswalk.disposition: Keep as a historical source-reported Paitan candidate. The name check does not independently verify the fish or its specimen-to-site link.

evidenceLimits: The publisher-indexed article text is partial; its direct PDF route returned HTTP 502 in the earlier access review.
No exact field collection dates, specimen accession numbers, institution catalog links, or row-level voucher records were verified for either Paitan candidate.
The catalog verifies nomenclatural status, not the identification of the article's specimens.
Historical evidence does not establish present-day occurrence, abundance, catchability, legal access, food safety, or fishing seasons.
No item-specific reuse permission was identified for the Silliman article; no figure, table, image, or numeric value was retained.
